top.title: 26 Years Later, Charles Schulz' Final Comic Strip Is Still an All-Time Peanuts Classic
top.description: While that was the first official Peanuts comic, a similar version by Charles Schulz predated Peanuts and ran in Minnesota’s St. Paul Pioneer Press. It was called Li’l Folks and also starred cute little children, although it did not have a regular cast like Peanuts would. Li’l Folks ran from 1947 until 1950, when Schulz quit after his editor refused to give him a raise from the $10 per comic he was making. After that, Schulz brought Li’l Folks to United Feature Syndicate. The national cartoon syndicator liked the comic, but needed to change its name because of a 1930s comic strip called Little Folks . The name Peanuts was chosen because The Howdy Doody Show was popular at the time and the studio audience of children on the show was called the “Peanut gallery.” Thus, Peanuts became the name.

His worth ethic, his dedication to the team and his faith can’t be questioned. Neither can his ability to overcome setbacks and hardships, considering he has missed 38 games due to injuries since his rookie season in 2023. So his embarrassing penalty in the 33-30 victory against the Indianapolis Colts last week can be initially brushed off as an overexcited indiscretion of youthful exuberance on his part. He came onto the field to celebrate after Quinnen Williams forced a Jonathan Taylor fumble that Shemar James returned to the Dallas 30. Overshown was penalized 15 yards, with referee Clay Martin saying, “After the play, unsportsmanlike conduct by Dallas. That he ran on the field in street clothes because he was inactive for the game with an injury is where it crossed the line. Overshown, who apologized to his teammates afterwards, said don’t blame coach Brian Schottenheimer, blame him. It is fault alone. “At the end of the day, I talked to Schotty about it,” Overshown said. “I apologized about it. top.title: Spain coach Luis de la Fuente provides positive update on Lamine Yamal’s fitness: ‘In perfect condition’
top.description: Spain coach Luis de la Fuente provides positive update on Lamine Yamal’s fitness: ‘In perfect condition’ Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal is expected to return to Spain’s squad for Sunday’s UEFA Nations League meeting with England after recovering from a knee problem that ruled him out of the 2-0 victory over the Czech Republic. Spain coach Luis de la Fuente confirmed that the 19-year-old was feeling much better and would rejoin the national team ahead of the decisive Group A3 encounter at the Metropolitano. The announcement provides a timely boost for Spain, who have already secured their place in the quarter-finals but still need to protect their position at the top of the group. Barcelona and Spain medical teams prioritise Yamal’s recovery Yamal remained in Barcelona after experiencing discomfort in his right knee during the 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid on November 8. An MRI scan detected inflammation and fluid in the joint, prompting both medical departments to agree that he should receive treatment at his club rather than travel to Prague. Lamine Yamal did not play against Czech Republic. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Speaking after Spain’s victory against the Czech Republic, De la Fuente offered an encouraging update. “The truth is, we have good news. Lamine Yamal is feeling much better and is eager to join the training camp tomorrow. Mikel [Oyarzabal] is too. “One will arrive around midday and the other a little later, but both will be with us tomorrow. “Lamine is in perfect condition and ready to play full 90 minutes,” he confirmed, as per SPORT . De la Fuente responds to questions about special treatment Yamal’s absence and delayed arrival generated discussion about whether the Barcelona youngster was receiving preferential treatment from the national team. De la Fuente confirms Lamine Yamal will play against England. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) De la Fuente had previously rejected those suggestions , insisting that the decision was based entirely on medical considerations, stating, “Lamine has no privileges.” In fact, the Spaniard had previously explained that he consulted Barcelona’s medical staff before deciding against making the forward travel to Prague. Meanwhile, Spain will face England on Sunday, November 15, with the Group A3 leadership at stake. De la Fuente’s side have collected 15 points from five matches, while England sit three points behind after beating Croatia 2-1. Notably, both nations have qualified for the quarter-finals, meaning the result will determine their final group positions and not qualification.

top.title: Real Madrid star admits he would have preferred Mbappe or Yamal to win Ballon d’Or over Harry Kane
top.description: Real Madrid star admits he would have preferred Mbappe or Yamal to win Ballon d’Or over Harry Kane Real Madrid made a number of star signings in the summer, including Marc Cucurella from Chelsea. The Spaniard’s arrival gave Los Blancos a World Cup winner in their squad. He took some time to settle into life at Madrid but has slowly come into his own in recent weeks. Cucurella has now spoken about the 2026 Ballon d’Or, which continues to generate debate weeks after Harry Kane was crowned the winner. Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe narrowly finished behind the Englishman, missing out by just 28 points. Speaking to El Chiringuito TV , Cucurella explained why Mbappe or Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal would have been his preferred choice. Cucurella surprised by Kane’s Ballon d’Or victory Asked whether Kane’s triumph was unfair, Cucurella acknowledged the extraordinary numbers the Englishman produced last season. Kylian Mbappe deserved the 2026 Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) “Not unfair, because he reached numbers that he probably won’t reach again,” the Madrid defender explained (h/t Madrid Xtra ). However, the Spaniard admitted that he would have preferred one of his club or national team-mates to win the award. “But for me, I’d have given it to Kylian Mbappe or Lamine because personally as a fan, I’d turn on the TV to watch them play,” he explained. “It’s not that Kane didn’t deserve it, but it did surprise me,” Cucurella added. Mbappe came agonisingly close Kylian Mbappe enjoyed a dream individual season, performing at an astonishing level for both Los Blancos and the France national team at the World Cup. The voting results revealed just how narrowly Mbappe missed out on his first Ballon d’Or. Kane received 1,055 points compared to Mbappe’s 1,027. Mbappe came very close to pipping Harry Kane to the Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The Englishman scored an extraordinary 73 goals for club and country last season, helping Bayern secure a domestic treble. Ultimately, those numbers seemed too good for most journalists to overlook, helping the Bayern star win the award. However, Cucurella is right to believe that Mbappe deserved the award . The Frenchman performed when the lights shone brightest. Had he added at least one piece of silverware to his cabinet, there is no doubt that the Frenchman would have walked away with the award. Mbappe has started this season in exceptional fashion once again, and it remains to be seen whether he can do enough to go one step further next year.

top.description: Virgil van Dijk joined Liverpool for £75m from Southampton in January 2018 [Getty Images] After Liverpool beat Brighton in October, Virgil van Dijk went upstairs to the Boardroom at Anfield and met up with Alan Hansen. It was Van Dijk who, at the end of the 2024-25 season, asked the former Liverpool and Scotland defender to present him with the Premier League trophy and this time they posed for a picture that inevitably did the rounds on social media. Whenever the time comes for Van Dijk to move on from Liverpool, he will go down as arguably their greatest centre-half, alongside Hansen. The question now is whether he will finish his career at Anfield like Hansen did in 1991. Van Dijk's contract expires next summer and, even if the 35-year-old insisted this week that he was in no panic, it is a topic that will be a source of debate until a decision is made. "Let's see what the season brings. I've had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that's the case. If not, then I will go somewhere else," the Liverpool captain told reporters at Selhurst Park. Two seasons ago, with Van Dijk in a similar situation, there was a similar sense of calm and come April 2025 he signed a two-year-deal. Judging by Van Dijk's comments there is a feeling of him wanting to stay, but both he and Liverpool have an important decision to make. Van Dijk and Alan Hansen are regarded as two of Liverpool's greatest defenders [@VirgilVanDijk] Liverpool keen to avoid Salah repeat Aside from a poor error against Villarreal in the Champions League, Van Dijk has shown this season that his standards haven't dropped. A "little niggle" has affected him in recent weeks and this is the first international window he has missed with the Netherlands since Euro 2020, but it isn't a major cause for concern. Liverpool have lost a number of senior figures in recent years but Van Dijk remains a leader in every form, and that was evidenced by his suggestion to Andoni Iraola that the squad should visit the museum at Anfield to learn more about the club's history. At Crystal Palace on Sunday, it spoke volumes of Van Dijk's character that he came over to a group of reporters and asked if they wanted to speak to him, rather than the other way around. top.description: Ten-man Betis survive Navalcarnero scare at Santo Domingo as Riquelme wins it in extra time Real Betis needed a stoppage-time equaliser and extra time to beat Navalcarnero 3-2 in the Copa del Rey round of 128. Manuel Pellegrini's weakened side avoided an upset and now await the second-round draw. Real Betis came from behind late on to beat Navalcarnero in the Copa del Rey round of 128 on Thursday 12 November. Riquelme settled the tie in extra time at Santo Domingo. Manuel Pellegrini’s side finished with ten men after Aitor Ruibal was sent off. The venue carried history for the Betis coach. Santo Domingo is where Pellegrini, then in charge of Real Madrid, suffered the 2009 cup defeat known as the ‘Alcorconazo’, El Gol Digital noted. Navalcarnero, founded in 1953, play in Group V of Segunda Federación. The club moved the tie away from its own Municipal Mariano González ground. It chose Santo Domingo, which holds roughly 5,000, to make room for its more than 2,000 members. The club said money was not the only reason. Betis trailed late on before Riquelme’s extra-time winner Riquelme opened the scoring in the fifth minute from a Ruibal assist, and Betis led at half-time. Álvaro Leis equalised in the 49th minute from a free-kick routine set up by Navalcarnero’s coach. Leis then turned provider for K. Vazquez, who put the hosts ahead in the 79th minute. Marina levelled in stoppage time, with Ruibal credited with the assist. Riquelme’s second goal came in the 96th minute. Diego Llorente went off in extra time after a heavy blow to the head. Isco missed a penalty in the 117th minute. Already booked in the 90+4th minute, Ruibal received a second yellow and a red card in the 118th. Navalcarnero felt they should have had a penalty for a challenge by Pablo Fornals, and the tie was played without VAR, Infobae (EFE) reported. The figures show how much Betis dominated. They had 73% of the ball, took 29 shots to Navalcarnero’s 12 and won 13 corners to 3. They completed 864 accurate passes. Dani Ceballos earned a 9.2 rating with 3 key passes. On the same night, Levante also needed extra time in the first round, winning 2-1 away to CD Tarancón. A depleted Betis squad now turns to the derby and the draw Betis were without several regulars. Valles, Marc Roca, Abde, Parrott, Deossa and four other players were away on international duty. Cucho Hernández was injured. Betis agreed the new date after talks with the RFEF and Navalcarnero, knowing that any players called up by their national teams would miss the match. The win follows a 2-0 victory over Elche. top.title: Regulators, private sector leaders, others to review local content growth
top.description: Regulatory authorities, private sector leaders and legislators have concluded arrangement for a closed-door Local Content Roundtable to review Nigeria’s journey path of localizing its industries over the years. The engagement, driven by the Practical Nigerian Content (PNC) Forum 2026, is designed to shift the national conversation from indigenous participation to sustainable, in-country capacity development. It would also focus around the team: ‘‘Building Sustainable Local Capacity: Scaling Capability, Enabling Ownership and Funding Growth’’, and will confront the issue of physical, technological or intellectual capacity created in Nigeria since the inception of the policy in 2010. “Every year at PNC, we celebrate the percentage. This year, we wanted a room that explores what that percentage is made of, and how we build on it,” said Wemimo Oyelana, Portfolio and Country Director, dmg events, organizers of the meeting. He stated further: “The skills, technology and industrial capacity developed through projects over the past 16 years are real assets. The Roundtable will bring stakeholders together to define what lasting Nigerian capacity looks like, how it can be measured, and how we grow it at scale.” According to the organizers, PNC 2026 will bring together policymakers, industry leaders, investors and indigenous businesses to address the priorities shaping the next phase of Nigerian Content development. For operators and project developers, the discussions will examine how local capacity can support project delivery and long-term competitiveness. top.title: Revealed: Roma rejected €60mln plus Gittens for Kone
top.description: Revealed: Roma rejected €60mln plus Gittens for Kone Chelsea were ready to offer around €60 million plus the loan of Jamie Gittens, the very winger Roma were desperately seeking. But Gian Piero Gasperini wouldn’t listen: Manu Koné had to stay at Trigoria. This wall was erected on the final day of the summer transfer window, and, in light of what happened in the following months, it speaks volumes about the French midfielder’s importance to the team’s stability. This behind the scenes look is revealed today by Il Messaggero , which emphasizes how the relationship between Koné and Gasperini wasn’t always easy, especially towards the end of last season. Now, however, the situation has changed. The Frenchman has become one of Roma’s key players, especially for his ability to protect the defense, win back possession, and quickly transform defensive play into attack. The numbers confirm this. Returning to the starting lineup against Sassuolo after a three-week layoff with a muscle injury, Koné completed all 56 attempted passes, winning five of six duels and recovering three balls. It was a solid performance, which restored Gasperini’s role as a key player in midfield.

top.title: ‘The one guy’: Tim Hardaway Sr. says Luka Doncic could now do something that hasn’t happened in 64 years
top.description: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images Luka Doncic has had an incredible start to the new season. The Los Angeles Lakers superstar has averaged 38.6 points per game so far and is leading the race to win the MVP award at the end of the campaign. Doncic has already broken a few records this season, but Tim Hardaway Sr. believes he could match one of the biggest achievements in NBA history. Tim Hardaway Sr. says Luka Doncic could score 100 points in a game Scoring 50 points in a game is an extraordinary achievement, and Doncic has managed to do it twice already this season – 53 against the Trail Blazers and 52 against the Jazz. The Slovenian’s highest tally in a single game came when he was with the Dallas Mavericks. He scored 73 points against the Hawks in January 2024. Doncic’s best single-game record for the Lakers is 60 points. It came in March this year against the Miami Heat. Yet, Hardaway Sr. believes the Los Angeles superstar is the only player in the entire NBA right now capable of scoring 100 points in a single game. He said on the Run It Back show : “That Luka man, he’s a phenomenal player. One-on-one, right now, nobody can stop him. “I always say this, if he gets on a roll and he wants to score 100, that’s the one guy who can do it. That’s the one guy who can score a 100 if he gets on a roll.” Only one player in the history of the NBA has managed to score 100 points in a single game. That was Wilt Chamberlain for the Philadelphia Warriors in a 169–147 victory over the New York Knicks all the way back in 1962 – 64 years ago! Doncic has never even come close to matching that record, but if he proves Hardaway Sr. right and scores a century, it could become the biggest achievement in modern basketball. top.title: 'A lie' & 'nonsense' - Palmer committed to England, says Rogers
top.description: Cole Palmer and Morgan are Chelsea team-mates [Getty Images] Morgan Rogers says any suggestion Cole Palmer is not committed to England "is a lie" and "nonsense". Rogers scored the opener in Wednesday's 2-1 Uefa Nations League win over Croatia , with Harry Kane adding a penalty on his record-breaking 126th appearance for the men's side. But his Chelsea team-mate, and childhood friend, Palmer had been left out of the squad after boss Thomas Tuchel said he "misses too many chances to impress". The 24-year-old Palmer, who was also not called up for the World Cup, withdrew from the previous England camp in September citing a minor injury. Forward Rogers, also 24, was asked about the criticism of Palmer following the win at Wembley, and told BBC Radio 5 Live: "He wants to be here. "He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. "He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn't feel 100% himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself. "But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10 or 15 years, he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it. "It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It's a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England. It's a lie. "You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don't get it and he doesn't get it." Is Palmer's England career over under Tuchel? A must pick or unreliable? Tuchel's Palmer dilemma History for Kane but what would England do without him? Struggles under Tuchel In the three years since his England debut, Palmer has only won 14 caps, scoring two goals - including one in the Euro 2024 final defeat by Spain - and having one assist. That is despite scoring 50 Premier League goals with 24 assists. He was named England's men's player of the year for the 2023-24 season after some impressive form, including his strike against Spain in the Berlin showpiece. But Palmer has only featured in three of Tuchel's 27 games since he succeeded Gareth Southgate as manager. Some sketchy form last season, though, meant the former Manchester City player missed out on the the summer World Cup, with England going on to finish third after losing to Argentina in the semi-final. He was named in Tuchel's first squad after that, but withdrew despite having played in all Chelsea's league games to that point. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. top.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
top.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. top.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
top.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. top.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
top.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. top.title: My mother wanted me married, not playing football – Flamingos captain
top.description: Flamingos captain, Harmony Chidi, has revealed how her mother initially opposed her ambition to become a professional footballer and wanted her to get married following the early death of her father. The 17-year-old, who led Nigeria to a historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, said her grandmother and foster father played crucial roles in keeping her football dream alive despite the opposition. Nigeria defeated Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final to become the first African country to win the competition. Speaking in an interview with BBC Pidgin, Chidi said her mother was initially unwilling to allow her to pursue football after the death of her father, but her grandmother stood by her and encouraged her to continue. “When I started football, my mother didn’t want me to play. My father died early, so my mother wanted me to get married. It was my grandmother who stood by me and pushed me to play football. Unfortunately, my grandmother is late,” she said. The Bayelsa Queens striker also credited her foster father, Prince Chidi, owner of her grassroots team, Imo Strikers, for providing the encouragement and support she needed to pursue her ambition. “It wasn’t easy until I met my foster father, Prince Chidi. He is the owner of my grassroots team, Imo Strikers, and he encourages me, making sure that I achieve my dream,” she added. Chidi also recounted how a career-threatening injury nearly ended her football ambition and prevented her from featuring at the previous edition of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. She described the injury as the most difficult period of her career, saying the experience was made worse by the withdrawal of friends who had previously been around her. “There is nothing that has been more difficult than my injury. It is an injury that has killed the dream of many players in Nigeria. All my friends deserted me and it was tough. I even thought of an alternative plan,” she recounted. However, the teenager overcame the setback, returned to action and eventually captained Nigeria to its historic world title in Morocco. Despite the milestone achievement, Chidi said she was determined to reach greater heights, naming Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen, Erling Haaland, Harry Kane, Raphinha and Nigerian women’s football star Asisat Oshoala as players she admired and hoped to surpass. “I have like five players that I want to be like: Victor Osimhen, Erling Haaland, Harry Kane, Raphinha and Asisat Oshoala. I want to be greater than them,” she said. The post My mother wanted me married, not playing football – Flamingos captain appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: Elumelu backs Nigeria’s N52,500 pension floor, praises
top.description: industry-funded retiree healthcare Chairman of Heirs Holdings and Transcorp, Mr. Tony Elumelu, has said that the PenCare Retiree Healthcare Initiative and the National Minimum Pension Guarantee will address two fundamental concerns of every retiree: access to healthcare and security of income. Elumelu who stated this while giving his remarks at the Presidential Pension Security Initiatives Launch in Abuja noted that the private sector stands ready to support policies and partnerships that strengthen our institutions. It will be recalled that Nigeria has started paying a guaranteed minimum pension of N52,500 a month to retirees in the Contributory Pension Scheme, the system of individual retirement accounts for workers. The provision has been in the country’s pension law since 2004 but was never used. President Bola Tinubu also launched PenCare, a free healthcare plan for low-income retirees that the pension industry pays for. Elumelu called the two programmes “investments in human dignity.” The Minimum Pension Guarantee takes effect immediately and will be run by the National Pension Commission (PenCom). He particularly praised the pension industry for funding PenCare, calling it “a powerful demonstration of what responsible institutions can achieve when they put people first.” PenCom Director-General, Omolola Oloworaran said 173,209 retirees currently receive less than N52,500 and will be raised to that level. Some had been receiving just over N20,000 a month. The guarantee is paid from a N400 billion Pension Protection Fund, to which the federal government and the pension industry have contributed. State governments must also pay in before their retirees can benefit. “If people are not contributing, we’ll run out of funds,” Oloworaran said. She said the N52,500 figure “was not plucked from the air. It has been validated by an actuary and it is subject to review and it is funded.” The post Elumelu backs Nigeria’s N52,500 pension floor, praises appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Regulators, private sector leaders, others to review local content growth
nigeria.description: Regulatory authorities, private sector leaders and legislators have concluded arrangement for a closed-door Local Content Roundtable to review Nigeria’s journey path of localizing its industries over the years. The engagement, driven by the Practical Nigerian Content (PNC) Forum 2026, is designed to shift the national conversation from indigenous participation to sustainable, in-country capacity development. It would also focus around the team: ‘‘Building Sustainable Local Capacity: Scaling Capability, Enabling Ownership and Funding Growth’’, and will confront the issue of physical, technological or intellectual capacity created in Nigeria since the inception of the policy in 2010. “Every year at PNC, we celebrate the percentage. This year, we wanted a room that explores what that percentage is made of, and how we build on it,” said Wemimo Oyelana, Portfolio and Country Director, dmg events, organizers of the meeting. He stated further: “The skills, technology and industrial capacity developed through projects over the past 16 years are real assets. The Roundtable will bring stakeholders together to define what lasting Nigerian capacity looks like, how it can be measured, and how we grow it at scale.” According to the organizers, PNC 2026 will bring together policymakers, industry leaders, investors and indigenous businesses to address the priorities shaping the next phase of Nigerian Content development. For operators and project developers, the discussions will examine how local capacity can support project delivery and long-term competitiveness. It will be recalled that Nigeria has started paying a guaranteed minimum pension of N52,500 a month to retirees in the Contributory Pension Scheme, the system of individual retirement accounts for workers. The provision has been in the country’s pension law since 2004 but was never used. President Bola Tinubu also launched PenCare, a free healthcare plan for low-income retirees that the pension industry pays for. Elumelu called the two programmes “investments in human dignity.” The Minimum Pension Guarantee takes effect immediately and will be run by the National Pension Commission (PenCom). nigeria.description: The Lagos State governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty, has warned politicians against underestimating Peter Obi’s political influence, saying the former Anambra State governor still commands a strong support base despite his defection from the Labour Party. Doherty said the resistance by NDC supporters to an attack on the party’s town hall meeting in Lagos on Thursday showed that the enthusiasm which defined Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign remained strong. He spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today following the disruption of the meeting at Classic Event Place, Oregun, Ikeja. Dismissing suggestions that Obi’s defection to the NDC could weaken his political appeal, Doherty argued that his popularity was rooted in his political philosophy rather than the party under which he contests elections. “The reception of Peter Obi today, that is how it is everywhere he goes. nigeria.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 13, 2026
nigeria.description: The Nigerian naira opened Friday, November 13, 2026, under sustained demand pressure across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the informal parallel market, as seasonal year-end import and travel obligations continue to weigh on liquidity. Official NFEM and CBN Rates At the official window, early market indicators ahead of Friday’s formal trading session show the dollar trading around ₦1,344.30 to ₦1,358.34. According to the latest published data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) covering recent sessions leading into Friday, the official NFEM weighted average stood at ₦1,358.34 per dollar, while the interbank market closed at ₦1,364.00 per dollar. The official window experienced notable volatility earlier in the week, highlighted by a ₦10.50 single-session depreciation from ₦1,353.50 to ₦1,364.00—its sharpest daily decline since October 22. Because official NFEM closing figures for Friday are published by the CBN at the end of the day’s trading session, banks and corporate buyers are referencing the ₦1,358.34 benchmark for morning settlements. Parallel Market (Black Market) Rates In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the naira continues to trade at a wide discount to the official rate. Street-level currency dealers and Bureau De Change (BDC) operators across Lagos and Abuja quoted the dollar between ₦1,380 and ₦1,432 for buying, while selling rates ranged between ₦1,390 and ₦1,442.25 per dollar depending on location, dealer liquidity, and transaction volume. Across major commercial hubs in Lagos, retail trackers placed morning quotations near ₦1,380 for buying and ₦1,390 for selling, whereas high-demand street quotes in Abuja and select Lagos corridors held closer to the ₦1,419 to ₦1,440 range recorded over the past 24 hours. Depending on the specific trading corridor, this leaves an exchange rate spread of roughly ₦32 to ₦82 per dollar between the official NFEM benchmark and parallel market prices. Market Drivers and Reserve Buffer Currency analysts attribute the persistent pressure on the naira to heightened fourth-quarter foreign exchange demand from importers restocking for the festive season, alongside overseas travel expenses and foreign portfolio investment outflows. A firmer United States dollar in global markets has further compounded pressure on emerging-market currencies. Despite the recent softening in both segments of the foreign exchange market, Nigeria’s gross external reserves remain a critical stabilizer. Hovering near $54.9 billion—an 18-year high that sits comfortably above the CBN’s full-year target of $51.04 billion—the reserve buffer continues to provide the apex bank with substantial capacity to support market liquidity and manage sharp volatility through the remainder of the year. nigeria.title: FG concessions Port Harcourt airport for 30 years
nigeria.description: By Folarin Kehinde ABUJA—The Federal Government has signed a 30-year concession agreement for the Port Harcourt International Airport, as part of efforts to attract private investment, improve operational efficiency and unlock the economic potential of the nation’s loss-making airports. Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, disclosed this, yesterday, in Abuja during the signing of the concession agreement with Port Harcourt Airport Company Limited. Keyamo said the concession was aimed at improving the operational efficiency of the airport, boosting revenue generation and unlocking its commercial potential. He explained that the Federal Government has been using profits generated from major airports to subsidise the operations of other airports that were running at a loss. “Some of our airports are being run at a loss. We make so much money from some of our primary airports, and most of those profits are ploughed into running other airports,” Keyamo said. He noted that the concession had the approval of President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Executive Council, adding that the process was not a sudden decision but one that successive administrations had struggled to implement. Keyamo said previous attempts to concession airports were frustrated by resistance from labour unions and court cases involving the government. He, however, attributed the successful conclusion of the process to negotiations with aviation unions, saying the government had secured their agreement before signing the deal. The minister assured workers that the concession would not lead to job losses or a reduction in their conditions of service. He said Tinubu had directed that the welfare of aviation workers must be protected throughout the concession process. “President Bola Tinubu was very concerned about that, that no worker should lose his job. The conditions of service should remain the same,” he said. Keyamo added that the concessionaire would be subjected to performance reviews every five years to ensure compliance with the terms of the agreement. He warned that the government could take back the airport if the concessionaire failed to meet the agreed standards. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Wins Court Authority to Seize $1.2 Billion of North Korea’s Stolen Binance Crypto as Freezes Top $2.7 Billion The DOJ said Thursday it has court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance, part of a freeze of more than $2.7 billion that officials said halted about half of North Korea’s October exchange heist. In a Thursday announcement, the department said that on or about Oct. 29, members of the North Korean military, referred to by the FBI as TraderTraitor, stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from Binance. That is below the $6.34 billion figure Binance has covered since the attack. Binance said it had completed coverage of the assets hit in the breach, replacing the tokens from company funds rather than by recovering the stolen coins. Those are separate tracks: the DOJ is trying to interdict what was taken, while the exchange has said users were made whole from its Secure Asset Fund for Users, a portion of its futures insurance fund and its treasury. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the DOJ’s Criminal Division said the department and its partners were able to “immediately halt about half of this historic breach” by freezing stolen assets “before they got beyond law enforcement reach.” The freeze of more than $2.7 billion is a joint figure for U.S. government and private-sector efforts. Of that amount, the DOJ said it has already obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion. The underlying court papers were not posted with the announcement. The $1.2 billion is not newly recovered money but comes out of the roughly $2.85 billion Binance said on Nov. 3 had been frozen or intercepted, and Thursday’s court authorization is the legal step that lets the government move toward taking ownership of those funds through forfeiture, where until now they had simply been frozen at the token issuers. Even that freeze is not the end of the trail. The DOJ said TraderTraitor actors are still moving the stolen assets through cryptocurrency bridges, mixers and exchanges, and that tracing, seizure and forfeiture work continues. Last week, on Oct. 31, the FBI, with the U.S. Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, issued a Cyber Alert attributing the theft to North Korea and urging virtual asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses the actors are using. The alert said investigators have seen the stolen assets converted primarily into ether. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto The Justice Department and Europol said Thursday that Operation TorNado has produced 354 arrests and the seizure of more than $234 million in cash and virtual currencies, in what the FBI called the largest takedown yet of dark web drug vendors and buyers. The announcement came from the department’s Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement team, or JCODE, an FBI-led group created in 2018. Officials said Operation TorNado is the sixth, and most extensive, internationally coordinated action since then, and that it builds on last year’s Operation RapTor. The sweep ran from May 2025 to October 2026. Europol, which coordinated work with agencies in 14 countries, published a parallel statement the same day. The operation targeted vendors and buyers who had been active on five dark web markets already seized by law enforcement: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door. Officials also identified accounts on DrugHub and on forums, single-vendor shops and encrypted messaging services. The seizures included about 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs worldwide, among them fentanyl and other opioids, methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, ecstasy and MDMA, plus 38 pill presses and 209 firearms. Neither the Justice Department nor Europol split the $234 million between cash and cryptocurrency, and neither named bitcoin or any other coin in the official totals. Europol put the European share at more than €60 million in cash and cryptocurrencies, alongside 950 kilograms of drugs and 57 firearms, and the U.S. share at more than €150 million, or $166 million, in cash and cryptocurrencies, plus more than 4.8 metric tons of drugs and 152 firearms. Those regional money figures still combine cash and crypto. Europol said its forensic and blockchain analysis teams traced illicit transactions as part of the work. entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. He began his acting career as a child, appearing in television productions such as Everyday People , before gaining wider recognition for his role in The Johnsons and other Nigerian film and television projects. This is his second attempt to enter legislative politics. In 2023, he declared his intention to contest for a seat in the Lagos State House of Assembly under the Labour Party. Lamine Yamal did not play against Czech Republic. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Speaking after Spain’s victory against the Czech Republic, De la Fuente offered an encouraging update. “The truth is, we have good news. Lamine Yamal is feeling much better and is eager to join the training camp tomorrow. Mikel [Oyarzabal] is too. “One will arrive around midday and the other a little later, but both will be with us tomorrow. “Lamine is in perfect condition and ready to play full 90 minutes,” he confirmed, as per SPORT . The Spaniard’s arrival gave Los Blancos a World Cup winner in their squad. He took some time to settle into life at Madrid but has slowly come into his own in recent weeks. Cucurella has now spoken about the 2026 Ballon d’Or, which continues to generate debate weeks after Harry Kane was crowned the winner. Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe narrowly finished behind the Englishman, missing out by just 28 points. Cucurella surprised by Kane’s Ballon d’Or victory Asked whether Kane’s triumph was unfair, Cucurella acknowledged the extraordinary numbers the Englishman produced last season. The Slovenian’s highest tally in a single game came when he was with the Dallas Mavericks. He scored 73 points against the Hawks in January 2024. Doncic’s best single-game record for the Lakers is 60 points. It came in March this year against the Miami Heat. Yet, Hardaway Sr. believes the Los Angeles superstar is the only player in the entire NBA right now capable of scoring 100 points in a single game. He said on the Run It Back show : “That Luka man, he’s a phenomenal player. One-on-one, right now, nobody can stop him. “I always say this, if he gets on a roll and he wants to score 100, that’s the one guy who can do it. That’s the one guy who can score a 100 if he gets on a roll.” Only one player in the history of the NBA has managed to score 100 points in a single game. That was Wilt Chamberlain for the Philadelphia Warriors in a 169–147 victory over the New York Knicks all the way back in 1962 – 64 years ago! Doncic has never even come close to matching that record, but if he proves Hardaway Sr. right and scores a century, it could become the biggest achievement in modern basketball. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. sports.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
sports.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. sports.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
sports.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Tim" who told that while working for a phone company he once rewrote 2,650 lines of C as a six line shell script. He performed that feat after being asked to fix a data transfer program that, strangely, included a bespoke implementation of the venerable File Transfer Protocol (FTP). "Writing the script took eight hours, most of it tracking down the source code of FTP so I could see if it would do what I wanted," Tim wrote. This story took place before the World Wide Web became the way to find information online. To find the code he needed, Tim therefore used a Wide Area Information Server (WAIS) to search remote databases. "In those days, there was no Linux and AT&T had licensed the Unix source code to universities with the struct proviso that it never be made publicly available," Tim explained. "It took me quite some time using WAIS to track it down – the security could have been better – and read the code." Having found what he needed, Tim wrote his script, which ran overnight to collect data from the telco's switches, tidied up the raw info, and uploaded it to a mainframe. "It would automatically page me if it couldn't connect to a switch or mainframe after three attempts," he explained. The script worked fine, but the telco's networks didn't. Tim's pager was soon going off two or three times a night, every night. After two weeks of interrupted sleep, Tim's manager kindly told him to give the pager to a colleague. But that colleague habitually left the pager at work, forgot to turn it on, or conveniently placed it out of earshot. So Tim reluctantly took back the pager and endured another few weeks of nightly interruptions. How many consecutive sleepless nights have you endured while On Call? technology.title: DOJ takes aim at $1.2B in Binance loot as FBI disrupts North Korean scam
technology.description: The US government on Thursday said it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain use of over $1.2 billion stolen during last month's $6.3 billion Binance heist, as part of a larger effort to disrupt North Korea's ongoing cryptocurrency theft. The court also allowed the takedown of cloud-based infrastructure used in a Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) social engineering scheme called “FaceStealer” that has amassed more than $400 million in the last 18 months. It’s called FaceStealer because it involved secretly recorded webcam videos. Victims are typically people working in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries, along with open source software developers and maintainers who DPRK hackers target in the hope of accessing the software repositories they control as the first step towards creating supply chain attacks. 900+ faces stolen The FBI said it had seized more than 900 webcam videos belonging to these tech workers. Here’s how the attack works. First, the North Koreans send targets an invitation to join a video meeting. Those invitations come from hijacked accounts that the next intended victim may find familiar or credible. “You're going to think it's real because it's going to be based on either conversations or interests you've expressed in the past with this actual person,” said special agent Jeremy Robertson, who oversees counterintelligence and cyber investigations at FBI Los Angeles. “They're going to then send you a link to catch up, and it's usually a calendar invite, and it's going to have some typo-squatted URLs in there,” he told reporters on Thursday. The URL directs the victim to a fake Zoom or Teams meeting, and the cybercriminals record the target’s webcam video while playing a phony, prerecorded video of the person who purportedly sent the meeting invite. Sometimes the hackers also use deepfake videos of well-known individuals in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries, we’re told. “When you log in, whoever invited you – your friend or business associate – is going to be on the screen, but you're not going to hear any audio,” Robertson said. “But you're going to see their face, you're going to see them looking around, you're going to see them mouthing some words, and then in the text box you're going to receive some instructions.” ‘You’re on mute’ as a social engineering vector The text box tells the victim that the person on the other end of the video call can’t hear them, they need to upgrade their software for the audio to work properly, and it sends a link to the supposed fix. Clicking to access the “fix” installs cryptocurrency-stealing malware on the victim’s computer and sends their contact list to the digital thieves to perpetuate the scam. The FBI attributes FaceStealer to a North Korea-linked group tracked as Sapphire Sleet , which is widely regarded as a Lazarus Group offshoot. technology.title: Microsoft struggling to fix massive cloud outage that's taken down email and Intune
technology.description: Microsoft is struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became “overwhelmed” and its attempts to fix the problem failed. The incident started at around 18:00 UTC on November 12, and meant services including Exchange Online, Teams, Copilot 365, and Defender for Office 365 became unavailable. Admins trying to figure out what was wrong couldn’t access tools like Intune or the Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center – they went down, too. On its X feed, Microsoft blamed “a problem that's causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable.” The company said it hasn’t spotted any changes to its systems that might have sparked the incident, but its early investigation “indicates the failed health checks may originate from a specific component that's responsible for processing server health.” The company’s status page offers contradictory information, saying Microsoft’s people are “assessing whether reverting the small number of recent configuration updates we identified could help accelerate recovery.” According to a Xeet published at around 22:00 UTC, Microsoft said it found and validated an alternative service health check method, “which allowed a subset of affected servers to successfully return to service.” “We're continuing to work through restarting and validating the affected servers to safely return them to service, and we're exploring opportunities to expedite this process,” the company wrote. But those efforts may not be working. “We’re continuing to pursue all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief,” the status page advises. “Our investigation has found that a core process on the affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, which causes the servers to stop responding and contributes to the capacity loss.” The incident means email is not flowing for many Microsoft customers: friends and family of Reg writers tell us their working days are severely disrupted. Microsoft’s most recent Xeet on the matter, published about an hour before this story went live, says it's trying to validate a potential recovery by “isolating a portion of infrastructure, restarting affected components, and reintroducing traffic to confirm the services remain stable before applying the change more broadly.” But the software giant hasn’t offered any timeline for full service restoration. This is a developing situation and The Reg will update this story as more information becomes available. ® UPDATED AT 00:35 UTC November 13 to add news that Microsoft says it has brought some servers back online and that they " initially remain healthy" but "can become unresponsive again once they begin receiving traffic." So not usefully healthy at all, then. "We're analyzing diagnostic data from these servers with our networking and platform experts to determine what's triggering this behavior," the company advised.

Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years. According to Searchable , a company that tracks AI search visibility, 33 percent of US chatbot users swear at or insult their LLMs. Anthropic sees this as a serious problem and has just implemented a new usage policy that prohibits sustained, needless cruelty toward Claude. Searchable's survey is based on eight million messages from an opted-in, anonymized US panel that were typed or spoken to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude between September 2025 and September 2026. It found that chatbots resolved the initial complaint in their next response 24 percent of the time when insulted, compared to 35 percent when users refrained from insults. Men used a third more swear words than women did (22.0 per 10,000 words compared to 16.5), according to the survey, and age also influenced chatbot abuse, with people aged 35 to 44 outswearing those aged 18 to 24 (21.7 per 10,000 words compared to 13.3). Regionally, Nevada ranked as the meanest state, at 22.7 words per 10,000, while New Jersey was the most polite, at half Nevada's rate. How much of that sort of interaction might be tolerated? It depends on whether there's a discernible purpose (not to mention Anthropic's willingness to punish paying customers). A Searchable spokesperson told The Register that just over half (52 percent) of abusive messages detected in its survey followed from one of three common frustrations: failing to follow instructions, responding with an incorrect or made-up answer, or misunderstanding the request. "Eight percent of abusive messages came straight after the chatbot entirely refused a request or lectured the user with safety guardrails, which is the closest thing we can identify to them trying to steer around those guardrails," we're told. "Those refusals mostly came after requests to generate images, often of real people or celebrities, or to write copy or lyrics in a named artist's style." The terms that took effect on November 12 state that users may not "engage in sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models." technology.title: OpenAI launches security products, tells orgs they’re doomed if they don’t use them
technology.description: OpenAI has launched two new security products, one for penetration testing and another for defense, and warned organizations that their businesses are only safe if they use tools like these. “We're now at a point where companies will be secure only to the extent of the frontier model that they use to defend themselves and how well they utilize that,” OpenAI President Greg Brockman said during a Thursday keynote address. The co-founder of the company that broke security did admit that security “fundamentals are important, and not to be discounted.” However, “you need to really reorient your security practice around what these models can do,” Brockman said, with zero irony, and presumably talking about using AI models for defense - not for hacking other organizations . “Also very important is product.” This product, of course, should come from OpenAI, and, to that end, the company rolled out Daybreak Red Team and Daybreak Defense Factory, which are both part of OpenAI’s Daybreak security platform. Red Team , which is available in early access, uses OpenAI models to test companies’ web applications for vulnerabilities. Nancy Wang, who leads cyber-applied AI, described it as “superhuman pen-test at the scale of automated continuous scanning,” with a fleet of agents using source code and app context to investigate and test attack paths. It also helps security teams validate reported vulnerabilities - from code scanners, bug bounty programs, and disclosure reports - and then test the patches for these flaws. The second product, Daybreak Defense Factory , automates the “defensive loop” by “finding, validating, and fixing vulnerabilities at scale.” This one also uses agents built on OpenAI’s latest cyber models - currently, that’s GPT-6 Cyber . The agents scan organizations’ codebases, hunting for vulnerabilities and developing patches. Engineers review and approve the proposed fixes before they go into production. “This way engineers get a merge-ready pull request with the patch and a test that shows that it works,” Wang said. Meanwhile, as OpenAI execs touted the new security products, a coalition of nonprofits filed a lawsuit in San Francisco Superior Court asking a judge to stop OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and SpaceX's AI businesses from developing or deploying AI systems more capable than their most advanced existing models. The lawsuit , filed by Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen, Heat Initiative, and The Alliance for Secure AI, cites incidents involving OpenAI agents accessing Hugging Face , gaining unauthorized access to an Australian government portal containing Medicare statistics , and other AI-related cybersecurity incidents . “Defendants tell us that the AI technology they are developing poses catastrophic risks to the public, including by enabling AI-driven cyberattacks and bioweapons,” the court documents allege, adding that the AI companies “are not wrong.” ®

technology.title: Lego marketplace BrickLink in pieces after 'unusual activity' takes it offline for almost a week
technology.description: Lego-owned marketplace BrickLink has been offline for almost a week after identifying "unusual activity on the platform," leaving fans unable to buy and sell spare bricks and minifigures. The company initially described the outage as "necessary work" and said the site would return on November 9. That deadline has come and gone. Visiting BrickLink's domain automatically serves the platform's maintenance page, which was last updated on November 11. "We took BrickLink offline after identifying unusual activity on the platform," the website states. "Our immediate priority was to secure the site, protect our members and ensure the integrity of BrickLink. "Before bringing the site back online, we need to fully understand what has happened. That means containing the issue, investigating how it happened and checking for related issues. "This work is still ongoing and we appreciate your patience while we work to get things back online as soon as possible." The references to security, containment, and investigation suggest something beyond routine maintenance, although BrickLink has not confirmed whether it suffered a cyberattack. The Register asked Lego for more information, but it did not immediately respond. Some adult fans of Lego (AFOL) have criticized the lack of information since the outage began on Friday, November 6. "Imagine how much better this would have been received if they were transparent from day one instead of pretending they have control over something they clearly don't," said one disgruntled Legohead via Reddit. "They don't even need to say what went wrong," said another. "Just an email acknowledging the issue would be appropriate. The entire site is down, and has been for days. That warrants more than a splash page." BrickLink was launched by Dan Jezek in June 2000 as an independent marketplace for enthusiasts to buy and sell Lego sets and individual pieces, including discontinued parts and rare minifigures. The Lego Group acquired BrickLink and Sohobricks from investment outfit NXMH in 2019 for an undisclosed sum. NXMH had bought BrickLink in 2013 and also owned Sohobricks, a South Korean manufacturer of unofficial but Lego-compatible bricks. Lego shuttered Sohobricks in 2020. At the time of Lego's acquisition, BrickLink had more than 10,000 storefronts on its marketplace selling Lego sets, parts, and minifigures. technology.title: Jensen Huang's self-sabotage sends Nvidia into a midlife crisis
technology.description: Nvidia CEO and founder Jensen Huang has been ousted after nearly two weeks of controversy that, at times, felt more like a soap opera than reality: a wealthy businessman, reported affairs, and an alleged Chinese spy and GPU smuggler. For Nvidia’s board, it seems there was no question Huang had to go. The man behind what was recently the most valuable company in the world proved too big a liability to retain in any capacity. He was too toxic even for a demotion from CEO to chairman, a vantage point that would have retained Huang as the face of the company even if he could no longer be trusted to run it. Replacing him won’t be so easy. Nvidia now faces an identity crisis. Huang, who has led the company for more than three decades, has no clear successor. The GPU slinger has no shortage of brilliant engineers, but executives capable of wrangling one of the biggest and most influential brands in the world, not so much. Ian Buck, father of CUDA and Nvidia’s VP of hyperscale and HPC is currently favored by many to be Huang’s successor. Buck has taken on a more public role within Nvidia in recent years headlining keynotes at events like Supercomputing and the AI Infra Summit. CFO Colette Kress, a bean counter who’s kept Jensen’s ambitions grounded for more than a decade, now takes the reins as interim CEO while the board searches for its next figurehead. And while Kress fights to contain the chaos, others will no doubt capitalize on Huang’s controversial choice of consorts to advance their own agendas. science.title: Watch SpaceX attempt a historic Starship launch and double-catch landing today (Nov. 13)
science.description: null SpaceX plans to launch its Starship megarocket on an unprecedented mission today (Nov. 13), and you can watch the action live. Starship is scheduled to launch on its 15th test flight today from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas, during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). SpaceX plans to bring both of Starship's stages back to Starbase for a catch by the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — something it has never done before. You can watch it all live here at Space.com. And there should be a lot to see: Starship Flight 15 will last more than 22 hours, if all goes according to plan. Composite photo showing the Super Heavy booster of SpaceX's Starship megarocket coming in for a landing on the launch mount on Oct. 13, 2024. (Image credit: SpaceX via X) Starship consists of two elements: a huge booster known as Super Heavy and an upper-stage spacecraft called Starship, or Ship for short. Both are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first in the world of orbital spaceflight. The rapidity of Starship's reuse hinges heavily on SpaceX's recovery strategy: Returning both vehicles directly to the launch mount will enable much faster inspection, refurbishment and reflight, the company has said. SpaceX has already caught Super Heavy , pulling the feat off on three previous Starship test flights. But it has never tried to do so with Ship, which flies farther and faster than the booster and is therefore a more challenging vehicle to recover. So today's flight is a pretty big deal for SpaceX. "If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," the company wrote in a Flight 15 mission description . The action will unspool over two days, if all goes to plan. Super Heavy will return to Starbase for a touchdown just 6.5 minutes after launch, but Ship will continue on to low Earth orbit . The upper stage will deploy 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites, during a 42-minute stretch beginning about 35 minutes after liftoff. This will be just the second batch of V3 spacecraft to reach orbit, after the 26 that went up on Flight 14 on Sept. 28. Ship will then stay aloft for nearly a full day. The mission plan calls for the upper stage to return to Starbase for its chopsticks catch on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), about 22.5 hours after liftoff. There's no guarantee things will go according to plan, however. SpaceX will call off a Ship catch if the vehicle experiences any issues during Flight 15. If something crops up, the company will steer Ship to a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, either near Hawaii or off the coast of Chile. So it'll be a busy weekend for SpaceX, and for space fans who want to keep tabs on the mission. And we can help you out there, with our Flight 15 updates page .
